correctness.rationale: Every partition has independent positive-pool indicators with negative probabilities u_G=product(1−p_i). Sorted blocks majorize all other vectors of log(u_G). Spreading two logs with fixed sum holds probability of at least one positive pool fixed and decreases probability of two; convolution/majorization transfer yields stochastic dominance of the entire test workload. Strict Karamata gives the full-law equality criterion. For pairs h(a,b)=ab(1−ab) has mixed derivative 1−4ab; four-point uncrossing gives the signed adjacent/opposite-extreme variance optima. Independently checked 942 exact tails and 246 pairing-variance evaluations. p_i=1 is a continuous limit only.

value.rationale: Workload upper-tail risk is a natural capacity constraint beyond mean assays, and the sharp 50% variance reversal warns that dominance does not imply variance minimization. Universal stochastic comparison plus distribution equality is mathematically useful independent of clinical deployment claims.
